record.original_question: Let f:(R^n,0)->(R,0) be a function germ with df(0)=0 and finite Milnor number μ(f), and let ρ(f) be the smallest number of real critical points among real Morsifications of f. Is every real Morsification of f connected to a Morsification with exactly ρ(f) real critical points by a generic path in the base of a versal deformation such that every A_2 Morse surgery along the path decreases the number of real critical points?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{R}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{R},0)$ be a smooth (or analytic) function germ with $df(0)=0$ and finite Milnor number $\mu(f)$. A real Morsification of $f$ is a real deformation $f_t$ of $f$ (lying in a versal deformation of $f$) such that, for $t\neq 0$ small, $f_t$ has only nondegenerate (Morse) critical points, all of whose critical values are real and distinct. Denote by $\#\mathrm{Crit}_{\mathbb{R}}(f_t)$ the number of real critical points of $f_t$, and define
$$\rho(f) := \min\{\#\mathrm{Crit}_{\mathbb{R}}(f_t) : f_t \text{ is a real Morsification of } f\}.$$
Inside the base of a versal deformation of $f$, the discriminant has codimension-one strata, and a generic real path crosses such strata transversally; the simplest real bifurcation along such a path is an $A_2$ Morse surgery, in which two real Morse critical points are created or destroyed (or, more generally, the number of real critical points changes by $\pm 2$).

Question: Given any real Morsification $f_0$ of $f$, does there exist a generic real path $\{f_t\}_{t\in[0,1]}$ in the base of a versal deformation of $f$, joining $f_0$ to a real Morsification $f_1$ with exactly $\rho(f)$ real critical points, such that along the path every $A_2$ Morse surgery strictly decreases the number of real critical points (i.e. the function $t\mapsto \#\mathrm{Crit}_{\mathbb{R}}(f_t)$ is monotonically non-increasing)?
